# Report information

Focused **advanced-quantification** report for immunopeptidomics experiments.
It compares peptide `Area` between Conditions: an unsupervised multivariate
overview (PCA, clustering, permutation test) followed by per-peptide
differential abundance with
[limma](https://bioconductor.org/packages/limma) moderated t-statistics, plus a
presence/absence track for the condition-exclusive ligands a quantitative test
cannot rank. The methods and the reasoning behind them are documented in the
*Methods & justification* section at the end.

`r HowMaHiCo::provider_line(params$Provider)`

**Sample Set:** `r params$SampleSet`

**Data Analysis: ** `r params$DataAnalysisNames`

**Date:**  `r Sys.Date()`

**Code version:** `r packageVersion("HowMaHiCo")`

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE)
if (!is.null(params$ProjectDir) && nzchar(params$ProjectDir))
  knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = normalizePath(params$ProjectDir, mustWork = FALSE))
```

```{r initialize, message=FALSE, include=FALSE}
# Running this report outside a knit (RStudio "Run All", or line by line)?
# Create `params` first:  params <- HowMaHiCo::report_params("05_quant_stats", ...)
library(HowMaHiCo)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(kableExtra)
library(ggpubr)
library(viridis)
library(plotly)
library(openxlsx)
library(DT)
```

```{r load-pep-all, message=TRUE, warning=TRUE}
# derives shortpep_range / palettes / output folders, loads (or builds) pep_all
# per PepAllSource, and derives pep_short + the grouping vectors - see
# ?report_setup for every object it creates
report_setup(params)
```


```{r quant-stats-prep, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=TRUE}
# ---- inputs -----------------------------------------------------------------
quant_input <- if (params$PeptideSet == "all") pep_all else pep_short
peptide_set_label <- if (params$PeptideSet == "all") "all peptides" else
  paste0("selected peptides (", shortpep_range[1], " to ", shortpep_range[2], " AAs)")

# limma is a Suggests dependency: fall back to the Welch t-test rather than
# aborting the render when it is not installed.
stat_method <- params$StatMethod
if (stat_method == "limma" && !requireNamespace("limma", quietly = TRUE)) {
  warning("StatMethod = 'limma' but the limma package is not installed ",
          "(BiocManager::install('limma')); falling back to StatMethod = 'ttest'.")
  stat_method <- "ttest"
}
norm_method <- params$NormMethod
if (!norm_method %in% c("median", "none") && !requireNamespace("limma", quietly = TRUE)) {
  warning("NormMethod = '", norm_method, "' needs limma; falling back to 'median'.")
  norm_method <- "median"
}

# ---- matrix, filtering, normalization, imputation ---------------------------
qm       <- build_quant_matrix(quant_input, feature = params$QuantFeature,
                               unit = params$QuantUnit)
coldata  <- qm$coldata
mat_raw  <- qm$mat
mat_filt <- filter_quant(mat_raw, coldata, min_per_group = params$MinReplicates)
mat_norm <- normalize_quant(mat_filt, method = norm_method)
mat_used <- impute_quant(mat_norm, method = params$ImputeMethod)

n_units_per_cond <- table(coldata$Condition)
# Keep only the pairs the chosen test can actually handle: a Welch t-test needs
# >= 2 units in both conditions, while limma pools the residual variance across
# the whole design, so it only needs >= 1 unit per condition plus at least one
# residual degree of freedom somewhere.
has_resid_df <- sum(n_units_per_cond) > n_conditions
testable_pair <- function(p) {
  n1 <- as.integer(n_units_per_cond[p[1]]); n2 <- as.integer(n_units_per_cond[p[2]])
  if (stat_method == "ttest") n1 >= 2 && n2 >= 2 else n1 >= 1 && n2 >= 1 && has_resid_df
}
contrasts_all <- if (n_conditions >= 2) comp_condition else list()
contrasts_list <- Filter(testable_pair, contrasts_all)
if (length(contrasts_all) > length(contrasts_list))
  warning(length(contrasts_all) - length(contrasts_list), " of ", length(contrasts_all),
          " condition pairs were skipped: not enough replicated units for the ",
          stat_method, " test.")
can_test <- length(contrasts_list) > 0 && nrow(mat_used) > 0

# ---- statistics -------------------------------------------------------------
diff_res <- quant_stats_results <- quant_stats_summary <- NULL
if (can_test) {
  block_var <- if (nzchar(params$BlockVar)) params$BlockVar else NULL
  diff_res <- test_differential(mat_used, coldata, contrasts = contrasts_list,
                                method = stat_method, block = block_var,
                                min_obs = params$MinReplicates)
  det_res  <- test_detection(mat_used, coldata, contrasts = contrasts_list)
  quant_stats_results <- combine_quant_results(diff_res, det_res,
                                               fdr = params$FdrCutoff,
                                               log2fc = params$Log2FcCutoff,
                                               min_detect = params$MinDetectExclusive)
  quant_stats_summary <- summarise_significant(quant_stats_results)
} else if (n_conditions < 2) {
  warning("Only one Condition in this subset — no differential comparison is possible.")
} else {
  warning("No condition pair could be tested: every Condition would need at least ",
          "one replicated ", params$QuantUnit, " to estimate a variance.")
}
```

**Peptide set:** `r peptide_set_label` &nbsp;|&nbsp; **feature:**
`r params$QuantFeature` &nbsp;|&nbsp; **unit:** `r params$QuantUnit`
&nbsp;|&nbsp; **normalization:** `r norm_method` &nbsp;|&nbsp; **imputation:**
`r params$ImputeMethod` &nbsp;|&nbsp; **test:** `r stat_method`

# Quantitative matrix

`Area` is summed over precursors within a sample, log2-transformed, then averaged
across the samples of each `r params$QuantUnit`. A feature is kept for testing
when it is quantified in at least `r params$MinReplicates` units of at least one
Condition; the features that fail the filter are still shown in the
presence/absence section.

```{r quant-matrix-table, echo=FALSE}
data.frame(
  Step = c("Features in the peptide set", "Quantitative matrix (features x units)",
           paste0("After filtering (>= ", params$MinReplicates, " units in >= 1 Condition)"),
           "Missing values in the filtered matrix"),
  Value = c(dplyr::n_distinct(quant_input[[params$QuantFeature]]),
            paste0(nrow(mat_raw), " x ", ncol(mat_raw)),
            paste0(nrow(mat_filt), " x ", ncol(mat_filt),
                   "  (", attr(mat_filt, "n_dropped"), " features dropped)"),
            paste0(sum(is.na(mat_filt)), " / ", length(mat_filt), "  (",
                   round(100 * sum(is.na(mat_filt)) / max(length(mat_filt), 1), 1), "%)"))
) |>
  kable() |>
  kable_paper("hover", full_width = FALSE)
```

```{r coldata-table, echo=FALSE}
coldata |>
  kable(caption = "Matrix columns and their annotation") |>
  kable_paper("hover", full_width = FALSE)
```

# Normalization {.tabset}

Between-sample normalization removes differences in HLA pulldown yield and
loading, which would otherwise be indistinguishable from biology. Compare the
distributions before and after: they should be centred on each other without the
individual spread being destroyed.

## Before (boxplots)

```{r plot-intensity-before, echo=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=5, warning=FALSE}

ggprint_rawr(p_intensity_before, interactive = interactive_plots)
```

```{r imputation-section, echo=FALSE, results='asis', fig.width=8, fig.height=5, warning=FALSE}
p_imputation <- NULL
if (params$ImputeMethod != "none") {
  cat("\n# Imputation\n\n")
  cat("Missing values were replaced using the `", params$ImputeMethod,
      "` left-censored scheme. The imputed values should sit at the low end of ",
      "the observed distribution, not inside it.\n\n", sep = "")
  imp <- attr(mat_used, "imputed")
  df_imp <- rbind(
    data.frame(Value = as.vector(mat_used)[!as.vector(imp)], Type = "observed"),
    data.frame(Value = as.vector(mat_used)[as.vector(imp)], Type = "imputed"))
  df_imp <- df_imp[!is.na(df_imp$Value), , drop = FALSE]
  p_imputation <- ggplot2::ggplot(df_imp, ggplot2::aes(x = Value, fill = Type)) +
    ggplot2::geom_density(alpha = 0.5) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = c(observed = "#440154", imputed = "#fde725")) +
    ggplot2::xlab("log2(Area)") + ggplot2::ylab("Density") +
    theme_howmahico() +
    ggplot2::ggtitle(paste0("Imputed vs observed values (", sum(imp), " cells imputed)"))
  print(p_imputation)
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

# Unsupervised overview

Before any per-peptide claim, does the quantitative data separate the conditions
at all? The PCA and the clustering below use only features quantified in every
unit (or all features when imputation is enabled).

## PCA {.tabset}

### Scores

```{r plot-pca-scores, echo=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=6, warning=FALSE}
p_pca_scores <- plot_pca(mat_used, coldata, type = "scores")
if (is.null(p_pca_scores)) cat("_Not enough complete features or units for a PCA._") else ggprint_rawr(p_pca_scores, interactive = interactive_plots)
```


## Heatmaps {.tabset}

The same `r params$TopNHeatmap` most variable features, drawn with and without
clustering: clustering shows whether the data group by condition on their own,
the unclustered view shows the conditions side by side in the annotated order.

In the clustered view the unit dendrogram sits above a Condition colour bar, so
you can see whether the samples split by Condition. The features are cut into
`r params$HeatmapClusters` clusters (`HeatmapClusters`), drawn as blocks
separated by white lines and labelled C1 (top) onwards next to the feature
dendrogram. With `CsvSave = TRUE` the feature-to-cluster assignment is exported
as `heatmap_clusters.csv`. The clustered view is a composite and stays static
when `InteractivePlots` is on.

### Clustered

```{r plot-heatmap-clustered, echo=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=9, warning=FALSE}
p_heatmap_clustered <- plot_quant_heatmap(mat_used, coldata, cluster = TRUE,
                                          top_n = params$TopNHeatmap,
                                          n_clusters = params$HeatmapClusters)
if (is.null(p_heatmap_clustered)) cat("_Not available._") else ggprint_rawr(p_heatmap_clustered, interactive = interactive_plots)
```

### Unclustered

```{r plot-heatmap-unclustered, echo=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=8, warning=FALSE}
p_heatmap_unclustered <- plot_quant_heatmap(mat_used, coldata, cluster = FALSE,
                                            top_n = params$TopNHeatmap)
if (is.null(p_heatmap_unclustered)) cat("_Not available._") else ggprint_rawr(p_heatmap_unclustered, interactive = interactive_plots)
```

## Global condition separation (PERMANOVA)

```{r permanova, echo=FALSE, warning=TRUE}
permanova_res <- NULL
if (isTRUE(params$PermutationTest) && n_conditions >= 2)
  permanova_res <- permanova_condition(mat_used, coldata)

if (is.null(permanova_res)) {
  cat("_Permutation test not run for this dataset._")
} else {
  data.frame(
    Statistic = c("pseudo-F", "p-value (permutation)", "permutations",
                  "complete features used", "groups"),
    Value = c(round(permanova_res$F, 3), signif(permanova_res$p_value, 3),
              permanova_res$n_perm, permanova_res$n_features, permanova_res$n_groups)
  ) |>
    kable() |>
    kable_paper("hover", full_width = FALSE)
}
```

# Differential abundance

```{r diff-design, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
if (!can_test) {
  cat("_Differential testing skipped for this dataset (see the warnings above)._")
} else {
  data.frame(
    Contrast = vapply(contrasts_list, function(p) paste0(p[2], "_vs_", p[1]), character(1)),
    Reference = vapply(contrasts_list, function(p) p[1], character(1)),
    Test = vapply(contrasts_list, function(p) p[2], character(1)),
    `Units reference` = vapply(contrasts_list, function(p) as.integer(n_units_per_cond[p[1]]), integer(1)),
    `Units test` = vapply(contrasts_list, function(p) as.integer(n_units_per_cond[p[2]]), integer(1)),
    check.names = FALSE
  ) |>
    kable(caption = paste0("Contrasts tested (", stat_method,
                           "); logFC > 0 means higher in the test condition")) |>
    kable_paper("hover", full_width = FALSE)
}
```

```{r plot-meanvariance, echo=FALSE, fig.width=7, fig.height=5, warning=FALSE}
# limma's mean-variance (SA) diagnostic: the trend that eBayes(trend = TRUE) fits
if (can_test && stat_method == "limma" && !is.null(attr(diff_res, "fit"))) {
  limma::plotSA(attr(diff_res, "fit"),
                main = "Mean-variance trend (limma SA plot)")
} else if (can_test) {
  cat("_Mean-variance diagnostic is limma-specific._")
}
```

```{r plot-contrasts, results='asis', echo=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=6, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
volcano_plots <- ma_plots <- pval_plots <- list()
if (can_test) {
  for (ctr in unique(quant_stats_results$Contrast)) {
    res_ctr <- quant_stats_results[quant_stats_results$Contrast == ctr, , drop = FALSE]
    cat("\n## ", ctr, " {.tabset}\n")

    cat("\n### Volcano\n")
    p_v <- plot_volcano(res_ctr, fdr = params$FdrCutoff, log2fc = params$Log2FcCutoff)
    print(p_v); volcano_plots[[ctr]] <- p_v
    cat("\n\n")

    cat("\n### MA plot\n")
    p_m <- plot_ma(res_ctr, log2fc = params$Log2FcCutoff)
    print(p_m); ma_plots[[ctr]] <- p_m
    cat("\n\n")

    cat("\n### p-value histogram\n")
    p_p <- plot_pvalue_hist(res_ctr)
    print(p_p); pval_plots[[ctr]] <- p_p
    cat("\n\n")

    cat("\n### Top features\n")
    top <- res_ctr |>
      dplyr::filter(Status != "ns") |>
      dplyr::arrange(adj.P.Val, adj.P.Val_det) |>
      dplyr::transmute(Feature, Status, logFC = round(logFC, 2),
                       AveExpr = round(AveExpr, 2),
                       adj.P.Val = signif(adj.P.Val, 3),
                       n_det_ref, n_tot_ref, n_det_test, n_tot_test,
                       adj.P.Val_det = signif(adj.P.Val_det, 3))
    if (nrow(top) == 0) {
      cat("_No feature passed the significance cut-offs._\n\n")
    } else {
      # kable, not DT: an htmlwidget printed from inside a results='asis' loop
      # needs an explicit tagList/knit_print dance to have its dependencies
      # attached, and silently renders empty when that is missed
      cat(utils::head(top, 50) |>
            kable(format = "html",
                  caption = paste0(nrow(top), " features with Status != ns (top 50 shown)")) |>
            kable_paper("hover", full_width = FALSE))
      cat("\n\n")
    }
  }
}
```

# Presence / absence

Features detected in one Condition and absent from the other. Their fold change
is undefined, so they are flagged by a detection rule (detected in at least
`r params$MinDetectExclusive` units of the Condition where they are present) and
the Fisher exact p-value is reported as supporting evidence — with few
replicates it cannot reach a small value even for a perfectly exclusive feature.

```{r exclusive-table, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
if (!can_test) {
  cat("_Not available for this dataset._")
} else {
  excl <- quant_stats_results |>
    dplyr::filter(Status %in% c("exclusive_up", "exclusive_down")) |>
    dplyr::arrange(Contrast, P.Value_det) |>
    dplyr::transmute(Contrast, Feature, `Present in` = Exclusive_in,
                     n_det_ref, n_tot_ref, n_det_test, n_tot_test,
                     P.Value_det = signif(P.Value_det, 3),
                     adj.P.Val_det = signif(adj.P.Val_det, 3))
  if (nrow(excl) == 0) {
    cat("_No condition-exclusive feature passed the detection rule._")
  } else {
    DT::datatable(excl, rownames = FALSE,
                  options = list(pageLength = 10, scrollX = TRUE))
  }
}
```

# Methods & justification

**Feature and unit.** The analyte in immunopeptidomics is the peptide itself —
HLA ligands are not tryptic peptides of an inferred protein, so no protein
rollup is applied. `Area` is summed on the linear scale across the precursors
(charge states, source files) of a feature within a sample, because charge states
are the same molecule, and only then log2-transformed. Values are averaged across
the samples of one `r params$QuantUnit`: with `BioReplicate` as the unit,
technical replicates collapse into their biological replicate instead of being
counted as independent observations, which would inflate the residual degrees of
freedom and make every p-value anti-conservative.

**log2 transform.** MS intensities are right-skewed and heteroscedastic; log2
turns multiplicative error into additive error, which is what a linear model
assumes. `Area == 0` is already mapped to `NA` by the loaders, so no zero becomes
`-Inf`.

**Normalization (`r norm_method`).** HLA pulldown yield varies by orders of
magnitude between samples, so without between-sample normalization a loading
difference is indistinguishable from biology. `median` removes only a per-sample
offset — the minimal assumption, and the default. `quantile`/`cyclicloess`
(via `limma::normalizeBetweenArrays`) additionally force the distribution shapes
to agree; that assumes most features do not change, which is a strong assumption
in an on/off ligand landscape, so it is offered but not the default. The
before/after plots above make the choice auditable.

**Filtering.** A feature is tested only when quantified in at least
`r params$MinReplicates` units of at least one Condition: a variance cannot be
estimated from a single value, and single observations in DDA are dominated by
stochastic precursor sampling. Requiring the minimum in *one* group rather than
all deliberately keeps condition-exclusive ligands, which the presence/absence
track handles.

**Differential abundance (`r stat_method`).** With `limma`, the model is
`~ 0 + Condition` with pairwise contrasts and empirical-Bayes moderation
(`eBayes(trend = TRUE, robust = TRUE)`). With the 3-5 replicates typical of an
immunopeptidomics experiment the per-peptide variance estimate is very noisy;
shrinking it towards a mean-variance trend fitted across all peptides increases
power and controls the FDR better than per-peptide t-tests (Smyth 2004; Kammers
et al. 2015). `trend = TRUE` accounts for the intensity-dependent variance of
label-free MS, `robust = TRUE` prevents a few wildly variable peptides from
inflating the prior variance (Phipson et al. 2016). limma fits each feature on
its observed values, so the matrix may contain `NA`s. `ttest` is an ordinary
Welch t-test per feature with BH adjustment — a Bioconductor-free fallback and a
sanity check against the moderated result. A blocking variable
(`limma::duplicateCorrelation`) can be set with `BlockVar` for paired designs or
when individual runs are used as columns.

**Missing values (`r params$ImputeMethod`).** MS missingness mixes MNAR values
(below the limit of detection) with MAR/stochastic ones (Lazar et al. 2016), and
in immunopeptidomics a large share is neither but genuine biology. Two tracks are
therefore reported: the quantitative test above, optionally after left-censored
imputation (`minprob`: per-sample down-shifted normal, mean - 1.8 sd, width
0.3 sd, the Perseus convention; `mindet`: deterministic low quantile), and a
Fisher exact test on detection counts for the exclusive features, whose fold
change would otherwise be an artefact of the imputation width.

**Multiplicity.** Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment within each contrast,
independently for the quantitative and the detection track. The p-value
histograms are the calibration diagnostic: a uniform histogram with a spike near
zero indicates a well-behaved test, while a hump towards 1 or a wave signals a
violated assumption and an untrustworthy FDR.

**Unsupervised overview.** PCA on the complete features, clustered and
unclustered heatmaps of the most variable features, and a distance-based
permutation test (pseudo-F on Euclidean distances between units, condition
labels shuffled `999` times; Anderson 2001) that answers whether the conditions
separate at all before any per-peptide claim is made. Note that the permutation
p-value is bounded below by the number of distinct label assignments — a 3-vs-3
comparison admits only 10 of them, so its smallest attainable p-value is about
0.1 no matter how clean the separation; read the pseudo-F alongside it.

*References.* Smyth GK (2004) *Stat Appl Genet Mol Biol* 3:1. Ritchie ME et al.
(2015) *Nucleic Acids Res* 43:e47. Phipson B et al. (2016) *Ann Appl Stat*
10:946. Kammers K et al. (2015) *EuPA Open Proteom* 7:11. Lazar C et al. (2016)
*J Proteome Res* 15:1116. Anderson MJ (2001) *Austral Ecol* 26:32.

```{r export-results, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Always-written exports: render parameters + the statistical results
write_input_params(params, folder = FolderResults,
                   prefix = paste(c(result_prefix, "05_quant_stats"), collapse = "_"))
if (can_test) {
  write.csv_rawr(quant_stats_results, folder = FolderResults, prefix = result_prefix)
  write.csv_rawr(quant_stats_summary, folder = FolderResults, prefix = result_prefix)
}

if (params$CsvSave) {
  quant_matrix_raw <- data.frame(Feature = rownames(mat_raw), mat_raw,
                                 check.names = FALSE)
  quant_matrix_norm <- data.frame(Feature = rownames(mat_norm), mat_norm,
                                  check.names = FALSE)
  write.csv_rawr(quant_matrix_raw, folder = FolderResults, prefix = result_prefix)
  write.csv_rawr(quant_matrix_norm, folder = FolderResults, prefix = result_prefix)
  heatmap_clusters <- if (!is.null(p_heatmap_clustered))
    attr(p_heatmap_clustered, "clusters") else NULL
  if (!is.null(heatmap_clusters))
    write.csv_rawr(heatmap_clusters, folder = FolderResults, prefix = result_prefix)
}

if (params$PlotsSave) {
  static_plots <- list(p_completeness_unit = p_completeness_unit,
                       p_completeness_feature = p_completeness_feature,
                       p_missing_heatmap = p_missing_heatmap,
                       p_intensity_before = p_intensity_before,
                       p_intensity_after = p_intensity_after,
                       p_intensity_density = p_intensity_density,
                       p_dynamic_range = p_dynamic_range,
                       p_imputation = p_imputation,
                       p_pca_scores = p_pca_scores,
                       p_pca_scree = p_pca_scree,
                       p_pca_loadings = p_pca_loadings,
                       p_heatmap_clustered = p_heatmap_clustered,
                       p_heatmap_unclustered = p_heatmap_unclustered,
                       p_sig_summary = p_sig_summary)
  for (nm in names(static_plots)) {
    if (!is.null(static_plots[[nm]]))
      ggsave_rawr(static_plots[[nm]], file = nm, folder = FolderFigures,
                  width = 20, height = 14)
  }
  for (ctr in names(volcano_plots)) {
    ggsave_rawr(volcano_plots[[ctr]], file = paste0("p_volcano_", ctr),
                folder = FolderFigures, width = 18, height = 14)
    ggsave_rawr(ma_plots[[ctr]], file = paste0("p_ma_", ctr),
                folder = FolderFigures, width = 18, height = 14)
    ggsave_rawr(pval_plots[[ctr]], file = paste0("p_pvalues_", ctr),
                folder = FolderFigures, width = 18, height = 14)
  }
}
```
